task: Task 1 — Selection authority extraction (key-based selection state + policy)
authorization: W1-P2 Task 1 GO from Lead directive (reuse existing engine; extract one verified key-based selection authority path; stop after harness + report blocker if none safe). Angular Wave 2 NO-GO. API-065/API-075 remediation NOT authorized.
nature: Characterization + parity evidence. No production source changed. No contract classification changed. No ledger/matrix change (129 records preserved).
conclusion: The key-based selection authority path is ALREADY fully engine-owned (flip commit e93eaea, ancestor of b3fb070). All selection mutations are computed by the pure engine (applySelectionRequest via transition); the component keeps _state.selectedIndices/_state.selectedItems as a DERIVED projection only, guarded dev-time by _assertSelectionProjection. No remaining transition can be safely (re)routed without either being a semantic no-op or a wider regression-risk change. Per the directive's stop condition, the task stops after the compatibility harness and reports this as the blocker.

blocker: Selection authority is already extracted as a single engine-owned path with a dev-time guard. The only remaining duplication (maxSelections pre-check at ~5616) is read-only (announcement) and removing it would change observable behavior. Range/visual-order computation is a platform concern; moving it into the pure engine would add DOM dependencies. A structural refactor is wider than 'one bounded transition' with regression risk and no benefit. STOP after harness.
